simulation.rationale: The task is a generic 'test task' with no specific domain, goal, or context. None of the files in the inventory provide any information about what the task actually entails. The always-on file CLAUDE.md is irrelevant because there is no concrete problem to solve, no codebase to navigate, and no decision to make. All agent and skill files are also irrelevant as they are designed for specific workflows (idea critique, skepticism, challenge planning, shipping checks) that have no connection to an undefined test task.

findings.title: Overlapping Agent and Skill Responsibilities
findings.detail: The 'skeptic' agent and 'ship-check' skill both claim the remit of adversarial review and checking implementation before submission, creating ambiguity about which should lead the process.

citations.quote: description: Adversarially reviews the implementation and agent workflow before submission. Use during ship-check. Returns BLOCKER / IMPORTANT / NICE-TO-HAVE findings.

description: Pre-submission gate for the 40-min challenge — build/typecheck, exercise the real workflow, adversarial review, autonomous browser test, fix blockers, deploy, summarize CHALLENGE_LOG.md. Run in the final ~10 minutes.

findings.title: Duplicated Validation Requirements
findings.detail: The requirement to validate LLM outputs and avoid 'vibes-based' or raw text consumption is stated in both the global CLAUDE.md and the specific skeptic agent instructions.

citations.quote: 4. **Validate generated outputs** — parse/schema-check every LLM output; retry-or-fallback on invalid. Never trust raw model text downstream.
3. **Poor validation** — LLM output consumed without parsing/schema checks, silent catch-and-continue, no fallback on invalid output.

findings.title: Redundant Planning Time Constraints
findings.detail: The 3-5 minute planning window is defined in both the skill description and the skill's internal rules, creating redundant instructions for the same task.

citations.quote: description: Rapid planning for the 40-min challenge — requirements → idea → architecture → acceptance criteria → implementation order. Target 3-5 minutes total, then start building.
- If planning exceeds 5 minutes, ship the current plan as-is.

findings.title: Contradictory Planning Duration
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md limits initial requirement inspection to 2-3 minutes, whereas the challenge-plan skill (which CLAUDE.md directs the user to use) allocates 5 minutes for the same phase.

citations.quote: 1. **Inspect requirements first** (2-3 min max) — read the brief fully before writing any code. Use `challenge-plan` skill.
Planning is a 3-5 minute sprint, not a document. Output goes at the top of CHALLENGE_LOG.md.

actions.rationale: Fold the skeptic agent into the ship-check skill to resolve remit ambiguity and eliminate redundant validation instructions.
The challenge-plan skill already covers adversarial review of plans; a separate agent creates unnecessary overhead.
Restrict to planning phase and resolve the 3-5 minute vs 5 minute internal redundancy within the skill definition.
Remove redundant validation rules already in skills and resolve the 2-3 minute vs 5 minute planning duration contradiction by deferring to the skill.
Essential for final validation; will serve as the single source of truth for adversarial review after merging skeptic.
